name: Glaze splashing
summary: Lead glazes of different colours are brushed, dripped or splashed on a fired body. They run together in the second firing and make streaks of amber, green and cream.
how: Fire the pressed body to about 1050 °C.
Brush or drip the coloured lead glazes on the biscuit.
Leave the base bare of glaze.
Fire again at 800 to 900 °C, so that the glazes run and mix.

origin.note: Tang kilns make sancai tomb figures and vessels with running lead glazes in amber, green and cream.

adoptions.via: Kilns at Gongxian and near Chang'an splash three lead glazes on horses, camels and court ladies for tombs.
